Merged in from EXP-71, a duplicate filed from the EXP-66 conversation and now withdrawn. Jack Heart, 2026-11-14: "Perhaps enabling the experiments we did with LLM-based players (both LMs that we run but especially LMs that are hosted behind OpenRouter or similar) may require additional changes and that can be a [follow-up] task"; sequencing: "the LOM stuff and the overrides, I would push those to be after the 4.1 release" (0.4.1, which waits for all of EXP-66). On hosted models: "In the case of the open router I think there's essentially no advantage to having an inference server over doing that [the job directly does the playing] and so that's probably what we should do" — so a hosted player is called from play directly, with no InferenceServer. On self-hosted: "I don't really think an inference server for Qwen is really any different than an inference server for the non-LLM models" — it uses EXP-73's InferenceServer(serve=...) (Manabot has manabot/llm/vllm_runtime.py). Thorns noted. Hosted: the API key must reach the machine without entering job records, identity or logs; no checkpoint, so identity is a model name that can change underneath; non-determinism; per-token cost invisible to rental dollar limits; rate limits and seconds-long latency against game clocks; API errors are infrastructure failures, not forfeits; tests cannot reach the network. Self-hosted: weights of tens of GB from outside Etude checkpoints, delivered inside the rental window; minutes of start-up; one LLM can fill a GPU. EXP-73 lets an eval job name more than one server because a match can seat an LLM against a checkpoint policy.
